title: How Many Pairs Add Up?

concept.title: Count the partners that came before
body: This is the "two numbers that add up" idea with counting. A number `x` forms a pair with every earlier number equal to `k - x`. Keep a map with the number of copies seen so far; before adding `x`, add `seen[k - x]` to the total.

The order matters: check first, then insert. Otherwise `x` could be paired with itself when `2 * x = k`. Because every pair is counted when its second element is read, each pair is counted exactly once.

statement: Count the pairs of positions `i < j` in an array of `n` integers with `a[i] + a[j] = k`.
hints: A pair is completed by its second element.
When you read `x`, add the number of earlier copies of `k - x`.
Insert `x` into the map only after counting.

explanation: Every pair is counted when its second number is read: the number of earlier copies of `k - x` is looked up in the map.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

seen = {}
total = 0
for x in a:
    total += seen.get(k - x, 0)
    seen[x] = seen.get(x, 0) + 1
print(total)
